transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what's been bringing you in today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because of work. It's just... dispatch and compliance. They've been tracking my route changes. Through the computer system, and... making these little comments on the radio. 

People keep saying it’s just normal oversight, but... I can tell. I know certain drivers are reporting on me. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
How long have you been noticing these things about dispatch tracking your routes and drivers reporting on you—days, weeks, or longer?

Um... I'm not sure of the exact day. But... I guess it's been really clear to me for about the past two months. With the computer tracking and... the things they say on the radio. So, yeah. Two months.
Besides the comments on the radio, have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people don't seem to hear?
No. Just... just the radio. I don't... I don't hear anything else.
Have you been using any alcohol, marijuana, stimulants, or other drugs recently, especially in the past couple of months?
No. I don't... I don't use any of that. Just coffee. That's it.
Before these past two months, would you say you've generally been a trusting person, or have you tended to be suspicious of others' motives for most of your adult life?

Um... I don't really know. I guess I was just... normal. 

I mostly just keep to myself, really. But I wasn't... I didn't think people were doing things behind my back before, if that's what you mean. I just went to work and did my job.

Aside from these concerns about dispatch and coworkers, have you noticed any changes in how well you're able to do your job, take care of yourself, or keep up with daily responsibilities over the past two months?

Um... I guess things are just... a little harder lately. I've fallen behind on some of the route reports at work. And... some of the drivers have been complaining, saying my instructions are confusing. I don't really know. 

And at home... my husband has had to take over most things. Making the meals, handling the phone calls... planning stuff. I just... I haven't really been keeping up with it.
When you first started noticing these concerns about dispatch and the drivers two months ago, did that feeling come on suddenly—within just a few days—or did it build up slowly over several weeks?
Um... I'm not really sure. I guess... it just sort of happened. I don't really remember if it was fast or slow. It's just... how it is now.
Have you noticed any changes in your motivation, energy, or interest in things you used to enjoy, or has anyone told you that your speech or thinking seems disorganized or hard to follow?

Um... I don't really know about my speech. Nobody said anything to me about it. 

But... I guess I just don't really do much right now. I don't feel like going to choir... or having the softball team over anymore. Mostly after my shift, I just... I sit at the kitchen table. I have the planner open, but I just... I can't really make myself start dinner. Or make any calls, or... anything. I just sit there.

Before these two months when the dispatch concerns started, did you notice yourself pulling back from activities like choir or softball, or losing energy and motivation, even a little bit, in the months leading up to that?

Um... I guess so. It didn't just start two months ago. It's... it's been a while. Maybe... eight months? 

I think... it started when they made me the temporary dispatch lead. Things just... started feeling different then. I just started pulling back, I guess.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with well-organized persecutory delusions (dispatch surveillance, coworkers reporting on her) lasting 2 months, accompanied by prodromal negative symptoms (social withdrawal from choir/softball, avolition, anhedonia) present for approximately 8 months total. There is clear functional decline in both occupational (falling behind on reports, confusing instructions) and domestic domains (husband assuming household duties). No hallucinations beyond ambiguous 'radio comments' embedded in delusional content, no disorganized speech reported, no manic/depressive episode overlapping the psychosis, and substance use is denied. The combination of prominent persecutory delusions with preserved relative coherence and the negative symptom prodrome meeting the 6-month duration requirement supports schizophrenia, paranoid type, over brief psychotic disorder or schizophreniform disorder.
